A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAT research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, figures and relocated sections support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original DAT classification, robustness and generation experiments on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet, plus appendix ablations, calibration, OOD detection and repeated-run results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds a CIFAR-10 noise-initialization experiment with quantitative results and generated samples.

M1.justification: v4 adds an optional variant that initializes contrastive PGD from uniform noise instead of auxiliary OOD images (Section C.5). The architecture, losses, two-stage training and ancestral sampling remain unchanged. Rewriting ascent on negative energy as descent on energy is mathematically equivalent.

E1.justification: Section C.5 adds a CIFAR-10 training and generation scenario without auxiliary image data, using uniform-noise initialization. The existing CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet, corruption and OOD-detection coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 and the matched appendix comparisons are unchanged, including JEM-family methods, EGC, RATIO and standard AT. The new experiment compares initialization variants of DAT.

E3.justification: The new noise experiment uses T=105 and PGD step size 0.4, versus T=50 and 0.1 for OOD initialization. Table 8 also changes DAT ResNet-50 (T=15) evaluation sampling from 14 to 13 steps, although Table 2 still lists 14. This establishes a reported setting revision, with an unresolved inconsistency, rather than evidence of rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: New Section C.5, Table 14 and Figure 15 test whether auxiliary OOD images are necessary, adding numerical and visual evidence for noise initialization. Existing component, augmentation, OOD-size, loss-weighting, corruption and norm-generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 19 and v4 Table 20 report identical means and standard deviations over five independent runs with different seeds, including zero divergences. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting procedure changes are documented.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 are unchanged. New Table 14 reports noise-initialized DAT with FID 13.72 and robust accuracy 74.03%, under its different PGD configuration. Table 7 revises CIFAR-10 FID from 9.07 to 9.12 and ResNet-50 FID from 6.86 to 6.87. The corruption table changes DAT T=50 FID from 7.19 to 7.57 (v3 Table 14; v4 Table 16).

T1.justification: Proposition A.1, its assumptions and proof, the support-versus-density characterization, and the implicit R1 derivation remain unchanged. Equation reordering, equivalent PGD signs and removal of a repeated sampling formula do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The three technical contributions and central claims of scalable robust hybrid modeling, competitive generation and faithful counterfactuals remain. The revised title and greater emphasis on intrinsic explainability restate capabilities already claimed in v3, including Section 4.3.2.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the noise experiment as showing that existing stability mechanisms can support training without auxiliary OOD images, while acknowledging worse FID. It also removes Figure 6's speculative attribution of RATIO artifacts to AutoAugment and drops the stronger causal attribution of OOD data efficiency to PGD exploration.

D1.justification: v4 supplies a code-repository link on the first page and documents uniform U(0,1) initialization and the noise variant's PGD settings. Existing hardware, training-time, checkpoint, augmentation and hyperparameter documentation is largely retained.

R1.justification: The Gao et al. (2018) multi-grid generative ConvNet citation and reference are removed. Appendix A.1 narrows its description of CEM from state-of-the-art generative performance to improvement over prior EBM methods. Most related-work expansion in Section 2 reorganizes material already present in v3's appendix.

P1.justification: v4 makes a broad editorial revision: it retitles the paper, rewrites substantial related-work and concluding passages, condenses explanations across the main text and appendices, merges Section 3.6 into Section 4.1, removes the concluding future-work paragraph, and adds acknowledgments and an appendix contents page.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 14 and Figure 15, groups Tables 1–2 on one page, moves Figure 8 alongside Figures 6–7, relocates Table 10, and removes Table 7's sampling-step column. Captions, heading typography and page headers change. Existing sample images and plotted evidence are retained.

improvement.justification: The new noise-initialization ablation addresses a previously untested dependency on auxiliary images and reports its generation-quality cost. The code pointer, appendix navigation and several corrected values also improve usability. These gains are limited: the new evidence covers CIFAR-10 with a larger PGD budget, a sampling-count inconsistency remains, and the main benchmark results and theoretical arguments are unchanged.
